name: xroar
why: A Dragon and Tandy 8-bit emulator lets you run and poke at vintage machine code and hardware behaviour.

brief.what_it_is: XRoar is a free emulator of Dragon and Tandy 8-bit home computers. The homepage says it emulates the Dragon 32/64, Tandy Colour Computers 1, 2 and 3, the Tandy MC-10, and some similar machines or clones. It runs on several platforms, with source code, Mac OS X, Windows, and Debian/Ubuntu packages offered. Its inputs are firmware ROM images and emulated disk or tape media, and its output is the emulated machine's display and sound. The homepage does not spell out the input and output formats in detail.
brief.why_it_exists: The homepage does not give a stated motivation. It presents XRoar as a maintained emulator for the Dragon and Tandy Colour Computer families, and it also links to a 6809 assembler, asm6809, for writing machine code for the Dragon.

commands_seen.context: Clones the XRoar git repository from the author's site, given in the Git repository download section.

brief.install_notes: Firmware ROM images are required to run the emulator usefully. The homepage says these can be extracted from a real Dragon, CoCo or MC-10, or obtained from the Dragon Archive or the Color Computer Archive. Other routes are a source tarball (xroar-1.12.1.tar.gz), prebuilt Windows ZIP or MSI installers in 32-bit and 64-bit, a 64-bit x86 Mac OS X binary, Debian snapshot builds in an Apt repository, and an Ubuntu PPA on Launchpad. Building from source has its own page in the manual, and there is a note on running under Wayland.
brief.standout: The homepage offers XRoar Online, a version that runs in a browser, so you can try a Dragon without installing anything. The version 1.12 notes also add GDB remote-debugging support for the emulated CPU, including MC-10 support, which suits people who want to inspect 6809 code and hardware state.
brief.status: Maintained. The homepage shows version 1.12.1 released 2026-07-27 and 'Updated 27 Jul 2026', with version 1.12 release notes listing new features such as SDL3 support and a new monochrome display option.
brief.caveats: Firmware ROMs are not included and must be obtained separately. The GTK+ 2 interface is deprecated in favour of GTK+ 3, and the author says they are unlikely to keep it working because Debian 13 shipped without the GtkGLExt packages it needs. The Android, AmigaOS 4, MorphOS and handheld ports are old and predate the 1.x releases, so they lack CoCo 3 and MC-10 support. The Mac build is 64-bit x86 only and was built under 10.13. The floppy disk image write-back behaviour changed in version 1.3. The license is GPL v3 or later, with no warranty.
quotes: XRoar emulates the Dragon 32/64; Tandy Colour Computers 1, 2 and 3; the Tandy MC-10; and some other similar machines or clones.
Firmware ROM images are required to usefully run this emulator.
